about.title: About
about.desc: What Relire Plus is and where your data goes.
about.what: Relire Plus is a close-reading assistant for French learners preparing for TCF Canada. Read real articles, open any word or sentence for an explanation, and practise saying them aloud.
about.privacy: There is no account and no app server. Your articles, vocabulary and recordings stay in this browser. When you use an AI feature, the text or recording goes straight from this browser to the provider you chose, with your own key.
about.scope: Relire Plus is a study aid. It has no mock exams and gives no official scores, and AI feedback is an estimate.

endings.title: Rule endings
endings.note: Underlined endings in the forms and this table come from the same rule. A dash marks a person not used in that tense.

present.name: Present
present.use: Use it for actions happening now, general truths, and regular habits.
present.form: Add the tense endings to the verb stem, such as -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent for regular -er verbs.

passeCompose.name: Passé composé
passeCompose.use: Use it for completed actions and specific events in the past.
passeCompose.form: Combine the present tense of avoir or être with the past participle.

imparfait.name: Imparfait
imparfait.use: Use it for ongoing background situations, descriptions, and repeated habits in the past.
imparfait.form: Add the endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient to the stem.

futur.name: Future
futur.use: Use it for actions or events that will happen in the future.
futur.form: For regular verbs, use the infinitive (dropping the final -e of -re verbs) and add -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont.

conditionnel.name: Conditional
conditionnel.use: Use it for polite requests, wishes, hypothetical situations, and advice.
conditionnel.form: Add the imparfait endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient to the future stem.

subjonctif.name: Subjunctive
subjonctif.use: Use it after expressions of necessity, doubt, emotion, wish, and judgment.
subjonctif.form: Preceded by que, add the endings -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent to the subjunctive stem.

imperatif.name: Imperative
imperatif.use: Use it to give direct orders, advice, instructions, or prohibitions.
imperatif.form: Use the present tense forms of tu, nous, and vous without subject pronouns; drop the final -s in the tu form of -er verbs, aller (va), and verbs like ouvrir (ouvre).

rules.er-regular: Standard -er verbs keep an unchanged stem throughout all tenses, as in nous parlons.
rules.er-cer: Verbs ending in -cer change c to ç before a and o to keep the soft sound, as in nous commençons.
rules.er-ger: Verbs ending in -ger insert a silent e after g before a and o to keep the soft sound, as in nous mangeons.
rules.er-yer-i: Verbs ending in -yer change y to i before a silent e, as in ils nettoient.
rules.er-e-grave: Verbs with e in the last stem syllable change it to è before endings with a silent e (and in the future and conditional), as in il lève.
rules.er-eacute-egrave: Verbs with é in the last stem syllable change it to è before endings with a silent e, but keep é in the future and conditional, as in je préfère.
rules.er-eler-double: Doubling verbs in -eler and -eter double l or t before a silent syllable and throughout the future and conditional, as in j’appelle.
rules.ir-issons: Regular second-group -ir verbs add -iss- in the plural present, imparfait, subjunctive, and present participle, as in nous choisissons.
rules.ir-sortir: Verbs like sortir and partir drop the stem’s final consonant in the singular present, as in je sors.
rules.ir-ouvrir: Verbs like ouvrir and offrir take standard -er verb endings in the present tense, as in j’ouvre.
rules.re-regular: Regular -dre verbs like vendre take -s, -s, and no ending in the singular present, as in il vend.
